More than a scholarship, the programme offers a unique development experience for New Talents, which includes:

  • An immersive talent development programme, in which scholarship recipients are mentored by tutors and a scientific committee, both composed of distinguished academics, who offer continuous guidance throughout the students’ research, nurturing excellence through close contact with excellence.
  • Scientific retreats – a unique experience combining scientific, cultural and social activities in the special environment of the Gulbenkian Foundation.

Learn more about the programme:

Conditions

The annual scholarship amount is made up of three components:

Research and study support – €1,000
To cover expenses related to further study and initial research activities.

Talent development support – €1,500
To support advanced training, participation in conferences, summer schools, internships, language courses, books, lab materials, and more. This amount is granted subject to approval by the scientific committee.

Supplementary social support – €2,000
Available to applicants whose household’s annual per capita income does not exceed €14,000. Applicants must submit proof of application to the Portuguese Directorate-General for Higher Education’s social support grants for the academic year 2025/2026. The Foundation will base its decision on the income figures assessed by this body.

Eligibility

Applications are open to students who:

  • Will be enrolled in the 2nd, 3rd or 4th year of a bachelor’s degree or integrated master’s programme, or in the 1st year of a master’s degree, during the 2026/2027 academic year at a higher education institution in Portugal.

The six-week festival took place at Mount Morris Park (today Marcus Garvey Park), in Harlem, New York City, and featured big names such as Stevie Wonder, Nina Simone, Sly and the Family Stone and B.B. King, amongst others.

Commonly known as the Black Woodstock, the Harlem Cultural Festival drew a crowd of 100 thousand people, although this historic achievement had been erased from the collective memory for almost 50 years.

item.description:
• Gulbenkian Orchestra

    In 1962, the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation decided to establish a permanent orchestral ensemble. Originally with only twelve musicians (strings and continuo) it was named “Orquestra de Câmara Gulbenkian”. This collective was successively enlarged and today the “Orquestra Gulbenkian” (the name it has adopted since 1971) has a permanent body of sixty instrumentalists, a number that can be expanded depending on the repertoire.

    This structure allows the Gulbenkian Orchestra to interpret works from the Baroque and Classical periods, a significant part of 19th century orchestral literature and much of the music of the 20th century, including works belonging to the current repertoire of the traditional symphonic orchestras. In each season, the orchestra performs on a regular series of concerts at the Gulbenkian Grand Auditorium in Lisbon, where it has had the opportunity of working together with some of leading names of the world of music (conductors and soloists). It has also performed on numerous locations all over Portugal, in an effort to decentralize music and culture.

    The orchestra has been constantly expanding its activities in the international level, performing in Europe, Asia Africa, and the Americas. In the recording field, Orquestra Gulbenkian is associated to labels as Philips, Deutsche Grammophon, Hyperion, Teldec, Erato, Adès, Nimbus, Lyrinx, Naïve and Pentatone, among others, and this activity was recognized with several international prizes.

    Hannu Lintu is the Music Director of the Gulbenkian Orchestra since 2023.

Missa Utica by Sammy Baloji is a performance that revisits the early contacts between Europe and the Kingdom of Kongo, intertwining colonial memory, spirituality, and music.

In partnership with Contemporânea, the CAM presents, at the intersection of live performance, concert, and artistic montage, Missa Utica (2024) by Sammy Baloji (DR Congo, 1978). The work brings together performers Fiston Mwanza Mujila, Pytshens Kambilo, and Barbara Drazkow Drążkowska in a dialogue with the historical ties between Europe and the Kingdom of Kongo. Memories of colonisation interweave with spirituality, colonial memory, music, and performance.

Based on extensive research conducted by Sammy Baloji on Congolese objects scattered across European collections, Missa Utica returns to the initial contact between Western Christianity and the Central African region, which occurred around the final years of the 15th century. Episodes linked to the evangelical religious conversion of the Kingdom of Kongo, colonial power dynamics, and the resulting cultural and political transformations are revisited within this context.

The title refers to Utica, an ancient Roman city located within the borders of modern-day Tunisia—a place chosen as a symbol, as it was there that the first African bishop of Black descent, Dom Henrique, son of King Afonso I of Kongo, was consecrated. This historical moment serves as a starting point to reflect on how European Christianity spread across the African continent and the relationships it forged with slavery, colonisation, and processes of cultural erasure.

A key highlight of the work is the Missa Luba, a liturgical composition created in the Belgian Congo in the 1950s by Franciscan missionaries, based on traditional Congolese musical styles. Although it gained visibility in Europe and the United States, little was said about the colonial conditions that allowed for its emergence. In Missa Utica, this past resurfaces, but now intertwined with Congolese rumba, recited verses, and improvised sounds.

Throughout the performance, music, text, and image merge into layers; different temporalities occupy the same space without hierarchy. Bodies speak for themselves, bringing forward histories of displacement, resistance, and survival. Voices emerge as traces of struggle and persistence against erasure. In this way, memory does not remain solely in the past—it reappears.

Rather than committing to a single format, Missa Utica blends elements of modern ritual with traces of sound performance. The work follows Sammy Baloji’s ongoing investigation into how colonial archives shape identities, historical narratives, and collective imaginaries.

Missa Utica is part of the Performance Program My Center is Not in the Solar System, under the artistic direction of Celina Brás and curated by Alexandra Balona.

item.title: Grants Gulbenkian Energy Communities Supporting renewable energy community projects in Portugal that empower citizens to play an active role in the energy transition. closes 16 Sep 2026 Open call
item.description:
Since Portugal introduced its first legal framework for collective self-consumption of renewable energy in 2019, community-led renewable energy initiatives driven by citizens, associations and local authorities have gradually begun to emerge.

Although Renewable Energy Communities (RECs) offer significant environmental, economic and social benefits, fewer than ten are currently operating in Portugal. RECs enable citizens to come together to generate, share, consume and store renewable energy, creating value both for their members and for the communities in which they operate.

In response to the absence of dedicated public funding for citizen-led Renewable Energy Communities, the Gulbenkian Foundation has partnered with Coopérnico – Sustainable Development Cooperative to support civil society organisations working alongside citizens, local authorities and other local stakeholders.

The initiative seeks to address some of the key barriers to establishing Renewable Energy Communities, including the upfront investment required to launch projects, limited technical capacity within local organisations and communities, and low levels of energy literacy among citizens.

Through this call, the Gulbenkian Foundation expects to fund 10 projects, with grants of up to €30,000 each.

Objectives

Grant funding will be awarded to projects that contribute to:

  • expanding decentralised renewable energy generation and local energy use;
  • strengthening the involvement of local authorities, community organisations and cooperatives in community energy initiatives;
  • promoting collective action through participatory governance models;
  • increasing the participation of economically vulnerable citizens and households;
  • encouraging Renewable Energy Communities in rural and low-density areas, while promoting greater territorial diversity;
  • fostering diversity and representation in project leadership and coordination.

Application process

The call for proposals will take place in two stages.

  • In the first stage, between 14 July and 16 September 2026, applicants are invited to submit an Expression of Interest outlining their proposal to establish a Renewable Energy Community, assessed on the basis of the proposed project and the profile of the lead organisation. The 20 highest-ranked applications will progress to the second stage.
  • In the second stage, between 19 and 30 October, the organisations behind the 20 shortlisted proposals will take part in a two-week online capacity-building programme. Following this programme, and based on the development of the proposals, 10 finalist projects will be selected to receive grant funding from the Gulbenkian Foundation.

Webinar

A webinar to present the call and answer questions will take place on 21 July, from 17:30 to 18:30, with prior registration required, including an open Q&A session.

Conditions

  • Grants are available only to legal entities established and registered in Portugal.
  • The amount awarded to each project will be determined during the final selection process and will not exceed €30,000.
  • Eligible costs include: administrative expenses associated with establishing a Renewable Energy Community; licensing procedures; the purchase and installation of renewable energy generation equipment for collective self-consumption and local energy sharing.

Eligibility

Applications are open to locally based, non-profit legal entities registered in Portugal.

This call is intended to support Renewable Energy Communities at an early stage of development. Therefore, at the time of application, organisations must not have a licensing application pending or already approved by the Directorate-General for Energy and Geology in Portugal; or have received funding from any public or private organisation for projects relating to Renewable Energy Communities or collective self-consumption.

How to Apply

  • Only applications submitted online will be accepted;
  • Register at  MyGulbenkian;
  • Before submitting your application form, check all the eligibility criteria and be sure to read the Call Conditions (available in the documents section);
  • Applications may only be submitted once all the mandatory fields of the form have been completed and the documents required under the Call Conditions have been uploaded;
  • Don’t forget to click “submit application”. Try not to submit your application in the last few days leading up to the deadline to avoid any unforeseen last minute problems.

Faq

Who can apply?

This call is open to civil society organisations that represent citizens' interests, are actively engaged with their local communities, and are committed to playing an active role in the energy transition through democratic participation.

Do members of a Renewable Energy Community need to be located within the same parish or municipality?

No. Under Portuguese legislation, members do not need to be located within the same parish or municipality. However, they must be located within 2 km of the renewable energy generation system (or 4 km in low-density areas), or be connected to the same electricity substation.

Can an informal group of citizens apply?

No. The Gulbenkian Foundation provides grants only to legally established non-profit organisations. An informal group of citizens may partner with an eligible organisation whose statutory objectives are aligned with this call, but it cannot receive funding directly from the Foundation.

Can a municipality or parish council apply? What about a local energy agency or another municipal body?

No. This call is intended to support citizen-led Renewable Energy Communities (RECs), meaning communities led by organisations representing groups of citizens, such as associations or cooperatives.

Municipalities, Parish Councils, local energy agencies and other municipal bodies may participate as project partners, but they cannot lead, manage or submit an application.

Is a recently established association, cooperative, foundation or other non-profit organisation eligible?

Yes.

Can an organisation submit more than one application?

No. Each organisation may submit only one application.

Are partnerships required?

No. However, partnerships formally confirmed through Letters of Support submitted with the application may strengthen the quality and feasibility of the proposal.

Are project partners required to make a financial contribution?

No. Partners may contribute in other ways, for example by making rooftops or other suitable spaces available for the installation of photovoltaic panels.

Can a research centre established as a non-profit private legal entity apply?

No. This call is not intended to fund research projects.

Can projects involve partnerships with for-profit organisations?

Yes. Projects may include local businesses or service providers with a relevant role in the community, provided that their participation falls within the scope of their corporate social responsibility activities rather than constituting a commercial service.

These organisations cannot become the sole owners of the project assets. Ownership must be shared.

Will certain territories be given priority?

Yes. Preference will be given to applications from low-density areas or territories facing greater social, economic or environmental vulnerabilities. Applicants should explain and justify these circumstances in their proposal.

Can an organisation that is already receiving funding from the Gulbenkian Foundation apply?

Yes. However, priority will be given to organisations that have never received, or are not currently receiving, funding from the Foundation. Projects that are already being funded by another public or private organisation will not be eligible for support.

Can the grant be used to recruit staff?

No.

What are the requirements for successful applicants?

In addition to managing the grant in accordance with the Foundation's funding rules, successful applicants must participate in all activities organised as part of this initiative, including the capacity-building programme delivered by Coopérnico.

They will also be required to submit a progress report after the start of the project and a final report, using templates provided by the Foundation.

Will there be an information session?

Yes. A free online webinar will take place on 21 July 2026, from 17:30 to 18:30 (Lisbon time). 

Can a national or regional organisation submit a project with a local focus?

Yes, provided that the proposal clearly demonstrates its local relevance.

Can project partners be changed after the application has been approved?

Yes, provided that the change does not compromise the objectives or successful implementation of the project.

Do the future members of the Renewable Energy Community need to be identified in the application?

Applicants should identify the prospective members of the Renewable Energy Community.

Can an organisation with no previous experience in the energy sector apply?

Yes. This call is intended for organisations that consume electricity, not for organisations already operating in the energy sector.

Should the project be selected, the organisation will need to amend its statutes in order to establish a Renewable Energy Community. The costs associated with this process are eligible for funding under the grant.

Can organisations based in the Autonomous Regions of the Azores and Madeira apply?

Yes. Organisations based in the Autonomous Regions are fully eligible to apply.

The only difference concerns the competent licensing authority. In mainland Portugal, the registration, prior control and licensing of Renewable Energy Communities are carried out by the Directorate-General for Energy and Geology (DGEG). In the Autonomous Regions, these responsibilities lie with the Regional Directorate for Energy (DRE) in the Azores and the Regional Directorate for Energy and Climate Change (or Regional Directorate for Energy) in Madeira.

What is meant by "vulnerable citizens or households" for the purposes of this call?

For the purposes of this call, vulnerable citizens or households are those experiencing financial hardship and at risk of energy poverty, as demonstrated by their eligibility for, or receipt of, the Social Electricity Tariff or the Social Natural Gas Tariff.

The aim is to support households for whom energy costs represent a significant financial burden and who stand to benefit most from the cost savings associated with participation in a Renewable Energy Community.

Does an REC have to be based on photovoltaic solar energy?

No. A Renewable Energy Community (REC) may choose other renewable energy generation systems. However, within the scope of this call, only solar photovoltaic generation systems will be considered, as they are currently the most cost-effective technology and the quickest to license and install.

Can a condominium (residential building or multi-family building) apply?

No. A condominium is not eligible because it does not constitute a formally established civil society organization.

Contacts

Questions about this call should be sent to: [email protected].

Before contacting us, please read the Call Conditions carefully and consult the Frequently Asked Questions, as your query may already be answered there.

• Gulbenkian Orchestra

    In 1962, the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation decided to establish a permanent orchestral ensemble. Originally with only twelve musicians (strings and continuo) it was named “Orquestra de Câmara Gulbenkian”. This collective was successively enlarged and today the “Orquestra Gulbenkian” (the name it has adopted since 1971) has a permanent body of sixty instrumentalists, a number that can be expanded depending on the repertoire.

    This structure allows the Gulbenkian Orchestra to interpret works from the Baroque and Classical periods, a significant part of 19th century orchestral literature and much of the music of the 20th century, including works belonging to the current repertoire of the traditional symphonic orchestras. In each season, the orchestra performs on a regular series of concerts at the Gulbenkian Grand Auditorium in Lisbon, where it has had the opportunity of working together with some of leading names of the world of music (conductors and soloists). It has also performed on numerous locations all over Portugal, in an effort to decentralize music and culture.

    The orchestra has been constantly expanding its activities in the international level, performing in Europe, Asia Africa, and the Americas. In the recording field, Orquestra Gulbenkian is associated to labels as Philips, Deutsche Grammophon, Hyperion, Teldec, Erato, Adès, Nimbus, Lyrinx, Naïve and Pentatone, among others, and this activity was recognized with several international prizes.

    Hannu Lintu is the Music Director of the Gulbenkian Orchestra since 2023.

item.description:
• Marisol Montalvo

    Soprano

    The American soprano is among the most sought-after exponents of contemporary music working today. She is possessed of an extraordinarily flexible instrument, “brilliantly stratospheric” yet “sweet-voiced”, that has enabled her to achieve success in repertoire from Strauss to Boulez. A consummate, “unstinting” singing actress, she has been greatly acclaimed for identifying unconditionally with her characters.

    As well as performing alongside many of the world’s most renowned conductors and orchestras, she has had the privilege of working closely with many of today’s leading composers, including Matthias Pintscher, Olga Neuwirth, and Wolfgang Rihm. Several have written roles especially for her, including Peter Eötvos (Sierve Maria in Love and Other Demons), Pascal Dusapin (Prothoe in Penthesilea) and Marco Stroppa (Olbia in Il Re Orso). Her affinity for contemporary music has led to regular engagements with ensembles including Klangforum Wien, Ensemble Intercontemporain, International Contemporary Ensemble (ICE), Ensemble Remix and Ensemble Modern.

    Although she has achieved success in a wide range of operatic repertoire, Montalvo is particularly associated with the title role of Berg’s Lulu. Following her debut in the part at the Opéra National de Paris, Le Monde described her performance as a true revelation: “The American soprano possesses real stage and vocal presence, and executes the exhausting role with incredible intensity”. Subsequently, Lulu has become the centerpiece of her stage work; she has performed it at houses including Deutsche Oper Berlin, Théâtre du Capitole Toulouse, Teatro de la Maestranza, Theater an der Wien, Komische Oper Berlin, and at Theater Basel, in the acclaimed production by Calixto Bieto.

    Outside the opera house, Montalvo has a particularly close working relationship with Christoph Eschenbach, who has been both a mentor and a regular concert partner throughout her career. Since conducting her Carnegie Hall debut with the Philadelphia Orchestra, he has invited her to work with him alongside orchestras including the Vienna Philharmonic, the Houston Symphony, the London Philharmonic, the Munich Philharmonic and the Orchestre de Paris. Most recently, she performed the role of Sophie in a concert performance of Der Rosenkavalier with the National Symphony Orchestra under his baton at the Kennedy Center in Washington, DC.

    She has also worked with conductors including Daniel Harding, Vladimir Jurowski, Christopher Hogwood, Yuri Temirkanov, Bernhard Kontarsky, Sylvain Camberling, Sussana Mälkki, Lothar Zagrosek, and Sir Neville Marriner, and with orchestras including the Cleveland Orchestra, the Los Angeles Philharmonic, the San Francisco Symphony, St Petersburg Philharmonic, DSO Berlin, SWR Sinfonie-Orchestra, RSO Wien, Finnish Radio Symphony Orchestra, and the Bamberger Symphoniker. She has performed at houses including Opernhaus Zürich, Bregenzer Festspiele, Gran Teatro del Liceu, Baden-Baden Festspielhaus, Teatro Real de Madrid, Glyndebourne Festival Opera, Theatre du Chatelet, Théatre de Geneva, La Monnaie de Munt, Opera de Monte Carlo, Lithuania National Opera, Polish National Opera and Opera Comique.

item.title: Grants Core Funding for Environmental Organisations Strengthening the capacity of organisations working to conserve nature and biodiversity. closes 07 Sep 2026 Open call
item.description:
In Portugal, more than half of all habitats are in decline. Civil society organisations working in nature conservation play a vital role in protecting biodiversity through the conservation, management and restoration of ecosystems. However, these organisations face significant funding and capacity challenges that limit the continuity and long-term impact of their work.

To help address these challenges, the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation launched the first edition of this programme in 2025, awarding core funding to eight environmental organisations. The programme demonstrated the value of core funding in strengthening organisations’ stability, independence and capacity to deliver lasting impact.

With this second edition, the Foundation is renewing its commitment to supporting organisations that play an essential role in protecting the environment and safeguarding Portugal’s natural heritage. By complementing traditional project-based grants, core funding gives organisations the flexibility to strengthen their capacity and pursue their mission in a more sustainable and effective way.

Conditions

  • Financial support will only be awarded to legally established entities registered in Portugal;
  • The amount of each grant will be determined during the final selection process and will not exceed €50,000.

Eligibility

Applications are open to organisations officially recognised as environmental organisations under the National Register, or equivalent organisations, as well as organisations working in the field of nature conservation whose activities align with the objectives of this call and which meet the eligibility criteria set out in the Call Conditions.

How to Apply

  • Only applications submitted online will be accepted;
  • Register at  MyGulbenkian;
  • Before submitting your application form, check all the eligibility criteria and be sure to read the Call Conditions (available in the documents section);
  • Applications may only be submitted once all the mandatory fields of the form have been completed and the documents required under the Call Conditions have been uploaded;
  • Don’t forget to click “submit application”. Try not to submit your application in the last few days leading up to the deadline to avoid any unforeseen last minute problems.

    The Gulbenkian Choir was founded in 1964 by the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation as a full symphonic body of around 100 singers. The choir joins the Orquestra Gulbenkian and other orchestras to perform Classical, Romantic and Contemporary choral-symphonic repertoire, but can also perform a cappella. It has performed – and often premiered – many 20th century works by Portuguese and international composers.

    Besides its regular season of concerts in Lisbon and frequent national tours, the Gulbenkian Choir has repeatedly toured Argentina, Belgium, Brazil, Canada, Denmark, France, Germany, Hungary, India, Iraq, Israel, Italy, Japan, Macao, Malta, Monaco, Netherlands, Spain, the United Kingdom, the United States of America and Uruguay.

item.title: Grants Portugal + Preparado Supporting a project that contributes to developing a culture of earthquake preparedness and resilience in Portugal closes 31 Aug 2026 Open call
item.description:
Portugal faces a significant seismic risk, particularly in the Lisbon and Algarve regions. Although recent earthquakes have served as a reminder of this vulnerability, public and political responses have often remained intermittent and reactive, rather than part of a sustained, evidence-based approach to preparedness.

As part of its 70th anniversary celebrations, the Gulbenkian Foundation is launching this call to support the design and implementation of a project that brings together science, communication and public action. The initiative seeks to strengthen connections between academia, civil society and policymakers, helping to build a more informed and resilient society.

The project should contribute to improving public understanding of seismic risk, strengthening the preparedness of families, schools and organisations, and supporting more effective public policies and decision-making in the field of earthquake preparedness and resilience.

An online information session will be held on 18 June 2026 at 11:00 (Lisbon time). Enroll: [email protected]

Conditions

The maximum support available is €250,000, including taxes and any other associated costs. Projects may have a duration of up to 18 months. Proposals must not exceed 12 pages, excluding annexes.

Indicatively, proposals may address one or more of the following areas:

  • Knowledge and public policy – organisation of conferences, working groups and other initiatives that contribute to knowledge production and the development of strategic recommendations for policymakers.
  • Capacity building and awareness raising – development of educational resources, training activities, communication campaigns, earthquake drills and other initiatives aimed at schools, professionals, organisations and the general public.
  • Pilot and demonstration projects – implementation of experimental actions that test innovative approaches, generate practical evidence and support their future integration into programmes or public policies.

Eligibility

Proposals must be submitted by a single coordinating organisation with recognised scientific and technical expertise in the field of earthquakes and seismic risk.

The coordinating organisation may establish and lead a consortium with other relevant entities, while retaining overall responsibility for the strategic coherence, partnership coordination and delivery of the project.

How to Apply

  • Register to apply;
  • Before submitting the application form, check all the eligibility criteria. We advise you to read the Call Conditions (available in the Documents area, in Portuguese only)
  • Applications can only be submitted once all the mandatory fields of the form have been completed and the documentation required by the Call Conditions has been uploaded;
  • After filling the form, click on the ‘submit application’ button. In order to prevent difficulties in submitting applications, avoid submitting your application in the last few days of the deadline.

After an intense journey through Mexico, Valentin Ceccaldi, cellist and founder of the Bonbon Flamme collective, returned home with the desire to compose music nourished by everything he had absorbed: the vibrant colours of nature and the streets, the acidity of lemons, the sweetness of avocados, the fire of chillies, the omnipresence of violence and death, and the relationship with ancestors and religion.

All of this is present in the quartet’s second album, Calaveras y Boom Boom Chupitos. Joined by three other incendiary musicians (Luís Lopes, Etienne Ziemniak and Fulco Ottervanger), Ceccaldi leads music with “a vast palette of colours” that adds “atmospheric pieces, occasional childlike melodies and a touch of ragtime”, according to UK Jazz News.

Magnificently delirious.

Improvised music, in the hands of its finest practitioners, resembles a fiercely contested sporting event with an unpredictable outcome. With the original quartet Canyon, it is easy to see that anything is possible.

Drummer Jerome Deupree provided the rhythmic backbone to the alternative rock of Morphine; cellist Lester St. Louis made his name in Jamie Branch’s Fly or Die; guitarist Joe Morris is, according to The Wire, “one of the deepest improvisers active in the United States”; pianist Sylvie Courvoisier is a colossus of inventiveness, described by Deupree as someone who keeps the group “on the edge of their seats, because the piano seems unable to contain her”.

In truth, everything in Canyon is unrestrained: the energy, the sonic exploration, the four-way communication, the vibration, the urgency.

Clear proof of his inexhaustible creative source, Joachim Kühn recorded the double solo album Échappée for Intakt Records shortly before turning 80.

Since the 1960s, the German pianist has been one of the leading figures in avant-garde jazz, thanks to an extraordinarily rich pianistic language that draws equally from the jazz tradition and the legacy of European classical music. This free and expansive world is fully present in Échappée, with Jazzwise highlighting the coexistence of references such as Ravel, Chopin, Bud Powell and Art Tatum.

“Do not expect calm, crystalline improvisation,” Jazzwise also wrote, “but rather a frenetic gallop which, after repeated listening, reveals an underlying sense of structure beneath the apparent randomness of cascading notes.”

item.description:
• Orquestra Juvenil Geração

    Orquestra Geração/Sistema Portugal was founded in 2007/2008 in Amadora through a partnership between the Municipality of Amadora, the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation and the Music School of the National Conservatory, inspired by Venezuela’s El Sistema.

    Over the past 18 years, Orquestra Geração has become a flagship project for social inclusion through orchestral music. Its success has been shaped by exchanges with Venezuelan teachers and conductors, the support of the Ministry of Education and the municipalities that have joined the initiative, as well as by private partners who share the conviction that music, the arts and culture are essential and irreplaceable in the full development of both societies and individuals, regardless of their backgrounds, beliefs or social circumstances.

    Today, the project reaches more than 1,700 children and young people, many of whom have gone on to pursue specialised music studies at leading institutions in Portugal and abroad.

  • Jose Jesus Olivetti

    Jose Jesus Olivetti is a young Venezuelan violinist and conductor who trained within the renowned National System of Youth and Children’s Orchestras and Choirs of Venezuela (El Sistema), where he began his musical journey at the age of eight. He studied violin with Savino D’Addona, Rubén Camacho and Francisco Díaz, and began his conducting studies with Tarcísio Barreto. He received training from Maestro José Antonio Abreu not only in orchestral conducting, but also in the design, planning and implementation of musical and orchestral projects. He later continued his studies in Europe with distinguished conductors including Jorma Panula, Colin Metters, Alex Treger and Maurice Hamers.

    Olivetti has participated in numerous international festivals and advanced training programmes, working with the Ruse Philharmonic Orchestra, the Burgas State Opera, the Berlin Philharmonic Chamber Orchestra and the Lithuanian State Symphony Orchestra.

    He has conducted major festivals and projects with Orquestra Geração in Portugal, as well as with national and international orchestras in Switzerland, Portugal, Spain and other countries. In 2023, he was among the winners of the Düsseldorf International Conducting Festival.

    As a conductor and guest conductor, he has collaborated with orchestras across the world, promoting access to classical music for international audiences.

    Alongside his artistic career, Jose Jesus Olivetti combines his musical activities with a strong social commitment. Through the Olivetti Foundation, which he founded, he develops projects aimed at supporting young talent, including the international competition Tocar y Luchar, sustainable support for orchestras in Angola and Mozambique, and specialised training programmes and lectures for musicians and educators in Medellín, Colombia.

    He also created the Meet the Community project, designed as a bridge between the orchestras he conducts, regional music schools and young musicians. The initiative promotes cultural, musical and artistic exchange, offering young people the opportunity to gain first-hand insight into the work and reality of a professional orchestra.

    Olivetti completed his studies at the Leopold Mozart College of Music of the University of Augsburg, where he studied conducting with Professor Maurice Hamers and violin with Professor Senta Kraemer. He was awarded scholarships by the Theodor Rogler Foundation in Germany and the Elena Probst Foundation in Switzerland.

    Jose Jesus Olivetti is currently Music Director of the Philludiker Orchester München, the Bodensee Ärzteorchester and the Garchinger Sinfonieorchester. He is also a violinist with the Seraphin Ensemble München and the Münchner Kammerphilharmonie Dacapo.
